messages:
Alex: Ran an nsys trace on the nightly perf job (batch mix: small S=256/S=512, variable seq). Seeing repeated KV cache write stalls during fused-flash attention. attaching a short summary.

Maria: ugh, that's the pattern we saw in canary last week, right? do you have the kernel timeline?

Alex: yup — main hotspots: 1) fused_flash_attn_kernel (write path) shows repeated SM idle gaps, 2) kv_write_coalesce kernel spikes, 3) lots of memcopy operations between device buffers. Perfetto slice shows small writes interleaved with compute.

Ranjit: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to replicate locally.

Alex: sure — ran:```nsys profile -o run.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu --force-overwrite --capture-range=kernel --nvtx true --stats true python -m perf.run_workload``` then converted with `nsys export --output run.sqlite` and opened in perfetto.

Devon: any nvprof counters? warp efficiency / shared mem stall rates?

Alex: grabbed a quick nvprof sample:```nvprof --metrics achieved_occupancy,warp_efficiency,sm_efficiency,shared_load_transactions ./bin/workload``` result (excerpt): achieved_occupancy ~0.58, warp_efficiency 72%, sm_efficiency 60%, shared_load_transactions high on the fused kernel.

PerfBot: automated trace note: detected repeated device->device mem copies (300+ in 60s) around timestamps 00:00:12-00:00:48. Possible small-chunk KV flush pattern.

Maria: that memcopy count screams small-chunk writes (non-coalesced). Is the KV write path using coalesced buffer or emitting per-entry copies?

Alex: code walkthrough: current path for small batches does `kv_write_async(entry)` per token; coalesce disabled for < BATCH_THRESH (default 8). So for S=256 with many tiny requests we hit per-entry writes a lot.

Ranjit: two angles: 1) batching heuristics -> lower coalesce threshold for high-concurrency routes, 2) kernel selection -> fallback to separate read/write-optimized kernel when write_coalescing==false. 3) prefetch stride tuning to avoid bank conflicts.

Devon: about bank conflicts — perfetto showed repetitive 64B stride on writes. On A100 L2 line size and bank mapping, stride of 128/256 can cause bank aliasing depending on layout. Can we try `prefetch_stride=128` toggle?

Alex: I ran a quick microbench: toggling `kv_prefetch_stride` from 64->128 reduced shared_load_tx by ~28% and increased warp_efficiency to 84% on the fused kernel for S=512 bursts. Latency p50 improved ~9ms.

Maria: nice. Any regression on large batch throughput? we must ensure we don't degrade peak perf for big S.

Alex: no measurable regression for S>=2048 in our test — maybe because large batches already use coalesced path. Problem is the mixed workload (many small concurrent requests) where kernel selection chooses fused-flash for memory locality but the write pattern kills occupancy.

Ranjit: propose heuristic change: if concurrent_small_requests>16 and avg_seq<=512 then force `kv_write_coalesce=true` and set `kv_prefetch_stride=128`. Also add a scoring rule in kernel selector: prefer write-optimized attn variant when predicted writes per micro-batch > X.

Devon: add a runtime switch `runtime.tunable.kv_write_backoff` that introduces slight delay to pack more entries into coalesced buffer before issuing device copy. Could trade a bit of tail latency for overall throughput.

Sara: ops question — how invasive is this? any on-disk format changes or backwards-incompatible?

Alex: no storage format changes. purely runtime buffering/heuristic changes and kernel selection flags. safe to roll as canary.

Maria: can someone prepare a reproducible perf job in the infra repro workspace and add a perf dashboard panel (per-kernel warp_efficiency, shared_load_tx, memcopy_count)? Then run baseline vs. kv_prefetch_stride=128 and coalesce forced.

Devon: I'll script a repro. plan: 1) reproduce with default heuristics 2) run with `--tune.kv_prefetch_stride=128 --tune.force_kv_coalesce=1` 3) collect nsys + nvprof metrics + perfetto slices 4) diff flamegraphs and csv metrics.

Ranjit: also capture KV cache timeline (per-shard) — we saw some shards doing hot write storms while others idle; could be imbalance from routing. Add per-shard counters.

Alex: noted. I'll upload the nsys exports and the perfetto screenshots to the thread. For immediate next step: Devon to run repro, Ranjit to prototype selector rule, Maria to add dashboard, I'll prepare a short RFC for the heuristic tweak.

PerfBot: reminder: please attach traces to the ticket #INF-4021 for trace retention.

Sara: thanks team — please @channel when the canary is ready. :thumbsup:

Alex: uploaded run.nsys and perfetto screenshots to #infra-artifacts (link). Will follow up with RFC draft later today.

Devon: started the repro run on repro-01 (ETA ~25m). will post results here.

Ranjit: I'll push a small change to kernel selector branch `ks/kv-write-score` with a draft scoring function, will tag for review.

Maria: great. if the 128 stride + forced coalescing fixes skew we can roll to canary and measure p95 tail for user routes.

Alex: thanks — logging action items: Devon (repro + traces), Ranjit (selector patch), Maria (dashboard), Alex (RFC + uploads).

Devon: repro finished. quick summary: default p50=58ms p95=290ms, tuned p50=51ms p95=210ms for mixed small-batch workload. attached nsys zipped export.

Maria: that's promising. schedule canary next week.

Alex: closing thread for now — will reopen if canary shows regressions.
